A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same registering/MITRE study. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching across reorganization and renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original EC-40 experiments, MITRE evaluations, fine-tuning results, ablations, and attention and representation analyses, including supplementary results in its appendices.

after.justification: V2 retains those empirical results and adds LAVS comparisons, LoRA fine-tuning results, and encoder-decoder registering experiments.

M1.justification: The core registering construction, attention mask, loss, and MITRE architectures remain unchanged. V2 adds an optional adaptation procedure using rank-8 LoRA components on query/value projections (Appendix E) and an encoder-decoder registering variant (Appendix J). These are limited extensions.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same EC-40/Flores coverage, 24-language pre-training corpus, and 5/25/100-direction fine-tuning selections. The multilingual attention cases are also retained. The added LoRA and backbone experiments reuse existing data and tasks.

E2.justification: V2 adds LAVS to the EC-40 comparisons at both model scales (Tables 1, 8, and 9). NLLB-3.3B also joins the fine-tuning comparison through LoRA in Table 4; previously it appeared only in pre-trained evaluation. Existing comparators are retained.

E3.justification: V2 adds parameter-efficient fine-tuning alongside full-parameter fine-tuning and introduces encoder-decoder registering controls at 12 and 24 layers. Existing splits and training budgets remain unchanged. Figure 5 changes its stated attention aggregation from averaging across layers to averaging across heads; this establishes a reporting revision, without establishing recomputation.

E4.justification: New Appendix J and Table 7 test whether registering's benefits depend on using an encoder-decoder or decoder-only backbone. The original register/mask ablation, length-ratio sensitivity study, representation analyses, and multilingual attention cases are retained; the latter appendices are renumbered.

E5.justification: The stated seeds remain 1234 for EC-40 training, 42 for MITRE pre-training, and 0 for direction selection. Neither version reports repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: V2 substantially extends the reported results with LAVS, LoRA across five models and three fine-tuning settings, and encoder-decoder registering. New MITRE-913M LoRA spBLEU scores are 28.14/31.68/32.33 for 5/25/100 directions (Table 4); encoder-decoder registering scores are 10.55/11.13 at 12/24 layers (Table 7). Shared numerical results remain unchanged; these are added conditions, not same-setting performance improvements.

T1.justification: The mathematical setup, cross-entropy objective, and generation equations (1–4) are retained. V2's new architectural and attention-dilution explanations introduce no formal assumptions, theorems, derivations, or proofs.

C1.justification: Both claim that registering reduces off-target translation without additional core model parameters, advances MNMT performance, and enables MITRE to compete with commercial LLMs while adapting effectively. The revised wording and additional LoRA evidence do not materially redefine these central contributions.

C2.justification: Appendix I replaces v1's semantic-knowledge and possible COMET-bias explanation with an output-style interpretation suggesting greater GPT-4o mini fluency. V2 explicitly qualifies this comparison in Section 5.3. New Appendix J adds parameter-efficiency and attention-dilution explanations for architecture differences; the formal limitations section remains substantively unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendices C and E add LAVS vocabulary and code details, a TDO repository link, and LoRA's target projections, rank, and trainable parameter counts. Existing EC-40/MITRE training configurations and model-release information are retained.

R1.justification: Related work is substantially reframed around explicit language-specific capacity versus implicit representation optimization, positioning registering as combining both. V2 explicitly identifies gisting/prefix-tuning as methodological inspiration, adds relevant citations including Rios, Li and Liang, and Hu, and removes the Vision Transformer registers and interlingua comparisons.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, method rationale, baseline descriptions, and mechanism discussion undergo extensive rewriting with more consistent MNMT-specific terminology. Related Work moves from Section 6 to Section 2 and is reorganized; the new architecture appendix shifts the existing supplementary analysis sections.

P2.justification: V2 expands the baseline and fine-tuning tables, adds Table 7, and changes Table 4's highlighting to distinguish LoRA and full fine-tuning gains. Figure 5 adds purple register borders and an expanded caption. Existing plots are retained with limited resizing and relocation.

improvement.justification: The added LAVS comparison, LoRA results including NLLB-3.3B, and encoder-decoder controls strengthen empirical support for the existing paper. V2 also makes the GPT-4o mini metric disagreement more explicit. The central results remain unchanged, and the new fluency and attention-dilution explanations remain indirect, so the overall quality gain is limited.
